newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB STICKS BY EARLIER FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: ABB STICKS BY EARLIER FORECAST.

text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said it was maintaining an earlier forecast that 1997 net profit would be at least as much as 1996's $1.233 billion.
"Net income for the full year of 1997 is expected to reach at least the same level as 1996," ABB said in its report on results after six months.
ABB first issued this forecast at its annual news conference in February and restated it when first quarter results were released in April.
Chief executive Goran Lindahl has described this forecast as a minimum for what profit could be expected for the full year.
Analysts on average forecast a 5.0 percent increase in ABB's 1997 net profit to $1.295 billion from 1996's $1.233 billion.
In its half-year report, ABB said a second year of economic slowdown in Western Europe continued to affect demand for many of the group's industrial and investment goods.
"Combined with the fact that demand for ABB's products and services trail late on average in the cycle, an upturn in ABB's West EuroPean markets is expected only during 1998," it said.
"However, strong growth in emerging markets and favorable effects of cost reduction programs are expected to have a positive impact on Group results," ABB added.
